findings.title: SLA status detail selection inlined 4× per operation instead of a named fragment
findings.failure: The same six inline fragments on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending/ImminentBreach/Breaching/Achieved/Breached/Cancelled are spelled out four times per file (once per target: firstResponseTime, nextResponseTime, firstResolutionTime, totalResolutionTime) and across three files — 72 inline spreads total. Any future field addition or rename must be applied 12 times, and a drift between the four copies inside one operation would silently give different shapes per target.
findings.evidence: services/mcp-server/operations/getBroadcastDetails.graphql:122-133 defines `fragment GetBroadcastDetailsActor on InternalActor` (a union) with inline member fragments inside, spread at lines 108, 113, 117 as `...GetBroadcastDetailsActor`. The same extraction applies to ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail (also a union, packages/core-graphql/src/schema.ts:14111-14116). lambdas/agent-sandbox-api/src/proxy/services/plain/fragments.ts:1-11 already keeps an SLA_FRAGMENT string for the same shape, confirming the team treats this as a reusable selection.

checked_fine: Schema types verified: ServiceLevelAgreementStatusSummary (packages/core-graphql/src/schema.ts:14119-14131) has firstResponseTime/nextResponseTime/firstResolutionTime/totalResolutionTime as nullable ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail; the union (schema.ts:14111-14116) has exactly the six members the inline fragments target.

Member field names match the schema: Pending/ImminentBreach have breachingAt( DateTime!), pausedAt( DateTime), remainingMinutesAtPause( Int) (schema.ts:14071-14088); Breaching has breachedAt (14089-14092); Achieved has achievedAt (14094-14097); Breached has breachedAt+completedAt (14099-14104); Cancelled has cancelledAt (14106-14109). All selected fields exist with compatible nullability.

Enum values in the getThreads.graphql comment match the schema: ServiceLevelAgreementStatus = {PENDING, IMMINENT_BREACH, BREACHING, BREACHED, ACHIEVED, CANCELLED} (schema.ts:14057-14069); ServiceLevelAgreementType = {FIRST_RESPONSE_TIME, NEXT_RESPONSE_TIME, FIRST_RESOLUTION_TIME, TOTAL_RESOLUTION_TIME} (schema.ts:6617-6621).
ThreadsFilter.serviceLevelAgreements: ServiceLevelAgreementFilter (schema.ts:6563, 6624-6628) accepts { statuses, types }; updatedAt is omitted by the PR but optional, so the input is valid.

Default-null slaStatuses/slaTypes yield serviceLevelAgreements = { statuses: null, types: null, updatedAt: null } after Zod defaults (packages/core-graphql/src/threads/threadsFilter.ts:58-71). The DB filter (packages/aggregates/src/thread/threadDbFilterUtils.ts:647-687 and 943-980) adds no SQL conditions when types/statuses/updatedAt are all null, so unfiltered getThreads calls are unchanged — confirms the PR description's no-op claim.

serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary resolver (packages/core-graphql/src/resolvers.ts:7761-7777) short-circuits to all-null without a query when parent.tierId === null && parent.serviceLevelAgreementPolicyId === null, so threads without an SLA pay no DB cost.

Resolver is dataloader-backed via reqCtx.serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDataLoader (packages/core-graphql/src/resolvers/serviceLevelAgreementStatusResolver.ts:14), so getThreads (10 results) and searchThreads (50 results) batch SLA status loads into one call per batch.

searchThreads returns ThreadSearchResult.thread: Thread! (schema.ts:13253-13255) and Thread has serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary: ServiceLevelAgreementStatusSummary! (schema.ts:13932), so the new selection is valid there.
getMyAssignedThreads.graphql and getCustomerThreads.graphql were intentionally not updated; PR scope is explicitly getThreadDetails/getThreads/searchThreads.
lambdas/agent-sandbox-api/src/proxy/services/plain/fragments.ts SLA_FRAGMENT is a separate consumer of the same schema path and is not affected by these MCP operation edits.

No in-repo snapshot or persisted-query fixture references getThreads.graphql/getThreadDetails.graphql/searchThreads.graphql by name; the only in-repo consumer is tools/graphql-lint/validateMcpOperations.ts, which validates against the core schema (all referenced types/fields/enums exist).

Rollback is safe: the change is purely additive — new optional variables default to null (no-op filter) and new response fields are additional; no existing MCP client depends on them, so reverting to HEAD~1 only drops the new SLA data.

No deploy/infra/migration/env-var/permissions changes; the diff is three .graphql operation files only, so there is no cross-system ordering, state-import, ForceNew, prevent_destroy, or CloudFormation export concern.
No shared constants, utils, or lists are modified, so blast radius is limited to the three MCP operations touched.
